The note supports E11.22. The assessment documents "Chronic kidney disease stage 3b, most likely due to type 2 diabetes." The note was written by a PA-C, an acceptable provider type, during a face-to-face visit.

The main risk is the phrase "most likely due to." In the outpatient setting, uncertain-diagnosis terms such as "probable" or "likely" cannot be coded as established. Here, though, CKD 3b itself is firmly documented and evaluated, with eGFR 43, losartan and empagliflozin continued, and nephrology follow-up. Only the causal link is hedged.

ICD-10-CM also presumes a link between diabetes and CKD under the "with" convention, unless the provider documents another cause. Here the provider attributes the CKD to diabetes, and nothing points to another etiology. The data are consistent, with persistent eGFR below 45 and albuminuria of 68 mg/g. E11.22 should be paired with N18.32.

Coders may disagree about the hedged wording, but the "with" convention supports the code regardless.

Counterpoints: the "with" convention would apply if no cause were stated, but explicit documentation of another etiology overrides it. Coding guidelines also treat hypertension and CKD as linked (I12.9), which fits the documented hypertensive cause. The elevated albuminuria (376 mg/g) and the diabetes could suggest diabetic kidney disease clinically, but the provider didn't document that. Coders can't infer it.

Some coders might still report E11.22 alongside I12.9, since a patient can have both, but that needs the provider to document both causes. The note states only the hypertensive cause. So the note does not support E11.22. It would support E11.9 or E11.65 (hyperglycemia is not explicitly stated, so E11.9 is safer), plus I12.9 and N18.31.
